pattern: Three of this round's four findings are sentences or fixtures the previous round *wrote*, not ones it left. That is the third round running in which the repair was wrong in a new way, and the shape is consistent: each replacement states the mechanism more precisely than its author had read it. `only when a look reports pending` is more specific than `Suspended with its volume` was, and wrong for a reason the old text never risked. The remedy is not more care in the same direction — it is reading the path the sentence describes before writing the sentence, which is what I did to find each of these and what the tester did to find the fixture asymmetry behind its own.

keyFindings.description: This change adds `|| volume.Ephemeral != nil` to the rig's volume mapping, so a pod's *ephemeral* volume is given `rig.tree` — the long-lived directory shared across pods — rather than the pod directory `run` allocates and deletes (`:251-253`). The rig therefore models the world this change abolishes: an issue pod's own disk aliases a disk that outlives it. Unlike the `issueSandbox` fixture the tester found, this one **branches today**: the cases at `:655-671` provision a second pod against the first's files, which selects the retained-clone paths (`internal/workspace/clone.go:245-251` skips cloning a complete clone; `provision.go:46-53,72-76` updates or restores an existing workspace). No issue pod inherits that state any more. The line was added by this change, so this is not a fixture it merely sits near: give an ephemeral volume a pod-local directory and let these cases prove fresh-disk isolation, keeping any retained-disk case that is still worth having as an explicit opt-in, as `internal/runtime/sandbox` already does with `withSupersededDisk`.

The comment written last round to replace a false one is false in a new way: it says `issueClose` releases the claim through the runtime, 'which under Agent Sandbox deletes the issue's Sandbox, and with it the pod and the pod's own disk'. It does not. `issueClose` calls `m.release` (`:1122`), `Machine.release` calls `Runtime.Release` (`machine.go:1041-1044`), and that implementation suspends the locator, forgets the claim and deletes a Sandbox only for the *controller's* claim (`runtime/sandbox/sandbox.go:769-780`, `releaseControllerSandbox`) — its own doc comment at `:765-768` says the issue's Sandbox 'is the tree cleanup's alone'. Whole-issue teardown is the separately fenced `IssueSuspend` effect (`runtime/sandbox/issue_suspend.go:52-63`). The distinction is exactly the one this round was fixing: at a merged child's close five claims get `issue_close` and no `IssueSuspend` is queued at all, which is why the implementer's pod survives.

The corrected `child-closed` sentence fixes the timing error I filed and introduces a condition that is too exclusive: 'the issue's Sandbox goes with the pod **only when a look reports `pending`**'. A first look reporting `pass` or `fail` closes the check, and `closeCheck` enqueues both the implementer's `issue_close` and an `IssueSuspend` (`internal/workflow/check.go:289-294`), so those delete it too; a `pending` whose wake is already queued starts the next look without deleting the pod (`:255-256`); and a look that ends with no report reaches the same teardown (`:220-230`). The accurate shape is that the merged close keeps the implementer and its pod for the first look, and the Sandbox goes when the check pauses between looks or closes — whichever outcome ends it. `packages/claude-envoy/legion/skills/legion-architect/SKILL.md:419-420` carries the same sentence. This is agent-read text about the architect's own lifecycle, which is why it is Important rather than prose.

The owned-volume remnants, including two more sentences this change wrote. Newly added and false: `podsafety.go:17` says 'no disk a pod mounts outlives it, the issue pod's being the pod's own ephemeral volume' — the controller's pod mounts a disk its Sandbox owns and which does outlive it, deliberately (`runtime/sandbox/podkind.go:308-325`); the claim wants limiting to an issue pod's disk and the probe's. Left standing: `supervise/table.go:1095` and `runtime/sandbox/sandbox.go:765` still attribute an owned volume to an issue Sandbox; `workflow/close_test.go:27-28` says every kind of child leave writes one `IssueSuspend` and takes the pod, where the same test asserts zero for the merged child at `:97-102`; `docs/kubernetes.md:4051-4057` still explains defending a carried-over issue volume whose feed an earlier agent replaced with a link, the scenario this round removed from `names.go`. With them, the tester's own two — `workflow/merge_close_test.go:215` and `daemon/outbox_issue_suspend_test.go:657`, both saying a Sandbox is released 'with its volume' — and the `issueSandbox` helper at `daemon/outbox_issue_suspend_test.go:83-89`, which builds `volumeClaimTemplates: [{name: issue}]` for five fixture Sandboxes. That one is bounded today because those tests suspend and delete rather than launch, so nothing branches on the template; it is worth fixing because `supersededDisk()` is true for any issue Sandbox carrying one, so the first daemon test that ever launches into these fixtures takes the migration path, passes, and proves the wrong thing.
